plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing dense, conical clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. It thrives in cold-winter climates and is a beloved garden staple in temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; widely cultivated across North America, Europe, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Lilacs can live for over 100 years and often persist at abandoned homesteads long after the buildings have vanished.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with large, showy, often double flowers and glossy, deeply lobed foliage. Its blooms are richly fragrant and make superb cut flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Peonies have been cultivated in China for over 1,500 years and are called the 'king of flowers'; ants on the buds are harmless and the plant does not need them to open.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial that carpets forest floors with nodding, bell-shaped flowers on arching stems. Mass blooms create a famous blue haze in ancient woods.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Native to western Europe, especially the British Isles, where about half of the world's population grows
plants.funFact: Bluebells are legally protected in the UK, where it is illegal to collect the bulbs from the wild.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in huge clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers, creating purple canopies and carpeting the ground beneath when petals fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacaranda trees earned it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'; in Mexico City, they bloom around spring, in March to May.
